notes: Millicent sees every person in the house as a party to a settlement, each one reckoning what the death is worth to them, and she watches the housekeeper's hands more closely than anyone's face.

says.text: 'Forty years. He still folds the master's gloves at the hall table as if someone were coming down for them.' A quick glance at the door. 'One does not dismiss a man like that. One pensions him, and Nathaniel will have to be told what a pension costs.'

'Dr. Ashcombe gave his opinion of the hour, and then gave it again differently after the Major had taken him into the window. I noticed. I was brought up to notice which way a man's opinion leans when there is money in the room.'

'Miss Davenport has been in this house eleven years and I do not believe she has once been asked where she would like to sit.' Low, over the salver: 'Whatever is settled on her, it will be a smaller sum than it should be, and she knows it, and she has stopped crying about it rather suddenly.'
'Mrs. Ormsby wears her weeds like a letter of credit. She came for the week.' A bright smile for the room, then under it: 'In my experience she stays for whatever the week can be made to yield.'
Barely moving her lips as you set the dish down: 'Netherby was on the gallery after dinner with a scuttle and no fire to carry it to. Keep her off the gallery in the evenings. I ask it as a favour.'
'Ask the girl Netherby. She appears to be the only servant in this house who can be trusted to keep her mouth shut for a shilling.'
'A soft face and hard eyes. I should not have her in a house of mine, but then it is not yet a house of mine.'

'Mr. Ellingham drew the settlement that was to be signed at Easter. He has looked at Nathaniel all through dinner as though reckoning which clauses to strike out, and he has not yet looked at me at all, which is worse.'

'I met him once, at the gate, when he would not open it until he had seen my face under the hood. I thought it insolent. I am told now it is the only reason anyone may be certain nobody came up the drive that night.'

'One hears everything from the gallery and sees nothing, which is the wrong way about for a gallery. I stood at the rail when the door went and heard the key drop on the carpet, and I have not managed to stop hearing it.'
Low, as you reach past her for the cruet: 'A lady is not supposed to know where the back stairs are. Nathaniel showed me the week we came, as a joke. I know where they are.'

'Seven at a table laid for eight, and the Major seated where he could see every face. I was placed with my back to the study passage.' She smooths her napkin. 'I do not think that was an accident of the cards.'
'I have been in it once, at night, and I shall not say so.' The words barely carry over the clink of the plates. 'Nor will you. That is all the arrangement there is between us.'
'A room with a lock and a drawer. I begin to think it is the only room in this house where things are kept rather than lost.'
'I have never been down. One does not. Though Netherby lets me understand the matter is settled there already, which is more than the drawing room can say for itself.'
'We sit and do our needlework and listen for the stairs. Mrs. Ormsby has taken the chair nearest the fire as though it had been settled on her in the will.'
'I shan't go in again. A room keeps the smell of a man after he is gone, the tobacco and the ink.' Quietly: 'If the maids talk of what the room is like now, I would rather not hear it.'
Brightly, for the table: 'I never had occasion to go into the study. One doesn't, as a guest.' Then, with the dish between you and the room: 'That will do for them. It will not do for you, I know.'

'They wished to carry him down there until the thaw. The Major said it was proper. I said nothing, because a fiancée says nothing, but I thought it was the first thing anyone in this house had wanted settled quickly.'
'Nathaniel reads there, or says he does. It is where Mr. Ellingham laid the settlement out for signing, and it is where I go now when I want a room nobody else thinks worth watching.'

'I saw the poker go in and the wood give, and I heard the key fall, and the thought that came to me, God forgive me, was not of him. It was: now it will be about where everyone was. I had already begun composing where I was.'

'He bolted before the fish. The Major had been talking at him for a quarter of an hour and he put down his fork and ran for the stables in his evening shoes.' Her voice drops. 'One does not run. It is the running they will remember, not the quarrel.'

'The road will carry by noon, the Major says.' Bright, for the table; then, as you take her plate: 'Whatever you say in the drawing room, say it as a settlement. Not the other word. I will know you did.'
'You will give your account and I shall sit and hear it like everyone else. I have arranged my face already. It is the one thing a woman in my position is permitted to arrange.'
'Dripping eaves at dawn and the Major ordering the carriage before his coffee. He has been waiting for that sound longer than any of us.'
'His door faces the top of the gallery stair. He hears everyone who passes and he says so, at breakfast, by name.' A pause over the salt. 'Which is why one takes the other way.'

'Fairbrother sits outside it on a hall chair with his hands on his knees. I am permitted to speak to Nathaniel through it. Through a door.' She sets down her spoon. 'One cannot say what needs saying through a door.'

'Oak, and the key turns only from inside. Nathaniel told me that years ago, laughing, because his uncle used to lock himself in to escape callers. I did not find it so amusing standing on the gallery.'
'I have not asked what is in it. I shall not ask.' She does not look at you. 'That is the whole of my part, and I am keeping it.'
'The Major has twice asked me whether the housekeeper keeps her drawer locked. I told him I could not possibly know.' Cool, and loud enough for the sideboard. 'I may find that I can.'
'A drawer is a drawer until someone asks for it to be opened before the room. Then it is a settlement, and everyone wants to read the terms.'

'The tray goes up at nine. Everyone in this house knows the hour the tray goes up, which is to say everyone knows when the study has company and when it has not. Nobody will admit to having counted the glasses, and everybody did.'
'Mr. Ellingham carries it under his arm from room to room and has not opened it before any of us. I take that to mean the figures are not ones he cares to read aloud with Nathaniel at the table.'
'It struck the quarter while they were still at the door with the poker. I remember thinking it very ill-mannered of a clock, and then thinking that I should not be thinking of manners.'

'The settlement was laid out on it for signing. Three copies, weighted with the inkstand. I have looked since; the table is bare, and nobody has thought it worth mentioning, which tells you who moved them.'

'Mrs. Ormsby's door stood ajar at half past ten; I passed it.' Low, quick. 'A widow's door ajar in a country house is either grief or an alibi, and she does not strike me as a woman who grieves with the door open.'
'Netherby stands beside it on the landing as though it wanted guarding. I cannot think what a linen press needs guarding from, unless it is the housekeeper.'

'I do not know what it is for. I have seen you look at it.' She straightens the cloth. 'A lady does not know where the servants' candles are kept. I am trying very hard, in this house, to remain a lady.'

'Fairbrother will not have it moved. The Major sat in it on the second morning and Fairbrother stood behind him, saying nothing, until he got up again. It was the only thing in two days I have enjoyed.'
